Such a fantastic entry in this venerable series of action games. From the visuals, sound, music, story and gameplay these elements come together to create a damn fine gaming experience that should really be played if you're a fan of the series. The opening credits alone will show you that clear as day. Highly recommended purchase, especially if you catch it on sale.

dmc 5 is just amazing. the gameplay, music, and graphics check so many boxes for me its not even funny. while the gameplay loop can on paper sounds like it would get stale, the three playable characters more than make up for it. each player plays vastly different. you have nero which plays similar to his dmc4 counterpart however with the added twist of having no devil trigger and a variety of mechanical arms that all have different effects. dante has his multiple weapons with different combos. and then there is V. V is complicated. while in the story his character is very interesting his gameplay may turn a lot of people off. V plays like a summoner. he has 3 familiars to fight for him. however they can not kill enemies and V must deliver the final blow with his cane. most of what V's gameplay translates to is mashing buttons while having him read his book to refill his devil trigger until an enemy turns white and then killing them. despite this the game is still impressive and a must play for fans. if you can find it on sale I highly recommend buying it immediately

This game absolutely deserves all the hype surrounding it. It will ask a lot from you while demanding very little on the starting difficulties which can lead detractors to be disappointed but I see it very differently. If you push yourself to improve and experiment you will be given an incredibly rewarding single-player experience. Co-op is completely nonexistent and no the Cameo System doesn't count. The soundtrack is remarkable and can be both heart pumping and serene even if it's very heavy handed. Despite having the option to buy basically God Mode and/or currency with real money the game itself never even mentions them nor did I ever feel obligated to. It's not a perfect game but its peaks more than make up for nitpicks. That Final Boss fight is one that I will remember fondly for a long time.

One of my favourite combat systems ever. While unfortunately it does force you to play the "normal" difficulty first, the higher difficulties that you unlock add more enemies and add lategame enemies early which really give you a great fight.

The normal/easy difficulties may be a fun experience for those who just like to relax and complete a game and leave it at that, there is a ton of fun for those who play through several times for a challenge. For those disappointed in the normal difficulty, see that as a tutorial, don't use revives and try for better ranks.

While it does have a couple of faults here and there, I highly, highly recommend this game for how good the combat is alone. This game is all about cheesy, over the top style.

reason.text: Negative reviews from this period mostly object to Capcom not bringing the Special Edition to PC, and reviewers describe PC players as second-class customers.
A news report from the same week says Capcom will not bring the Special Edition to PC, matching reviews that point to its focus on consoles.

lines.F1: Devil May Cry 5 had a score drop (the monthly score fell well below its usual level), Sep 2020
lines.F2: Sep 2020: 60% positive across 672 reviews (269 negative), against a usual 94% positive and 16 negative a month
lines.R1: (negative review, 34h played) "I love this game, don't buy it. Unless Capcom stops treating us like dirty second class citizens that don't get the Special Edition despite overwhelming fan support for the game on PC and two years of free advertising with all our combo videos and..."
lines.R4: (negative review, 93h played) "This game by itself absolutely deserves a thumb up. Unfortunately, Capcom's decided to get greedy and not give us Special Edition on PC. We're getting Vergil DLC, but not a new difficulty, or Turbo mode, or performance upgrades, or increased FPS, or..."
lines.R5: (negative review, 33h played) "One of the freshest and most fun action game I've ever played, but Capcom views PC customers as second-rate. I'm not whining that the PC version isn't some superior version and need to have dominion over consoles. Forget that. I just think that..."
lines.R7: (negative review, 35h played) "[quote=Capcom] Devil May Cry 5 Special Edition is specifically being developed and optimised to benefit the system architecture and leap in processing power offered by PS5 and Xbox Series X, so we’re focusing on these platforms. At present, there..."
lines.N3: 2020-09-17, Eurogamer: Capcom says Devil May Cry 5 Special Edition won't come to PC

news.title: Capcom says Devil May Cry 5 Special Edition won't come to PC

tldr.text: Overwhelmingly Positive (95%): 51% of reviews praise the story and characters, and the combat draws praise too.
The story and combat draw the most complaints, while the price draws fewer.

details.text: New players are far less positive, at 73%, than long-time players, who sit at 97%.
A flagged dip in the past dropped the monthly score to 60%, but recent reviews are about the same as the all-time score.
